I pushed compatibility code. It's somewhat awkward, because the usual workflow with main screens is that you add the dock as a child of a dedicated node and its data is available via virtual methods in EditorPlugin. I replaced that special control with a new one that intercepts added children and moves them to a dock. Unfortunately there are edge cases that are not 100% compatible:
- You need to add the main screen control in plugin's `_enter_tree()` or related callback. This is usually a case, but I have a main screen plugin that waits one frame before adding. It broke xd
- You can no longer remove the main screen control from the "dedicated main screen parent", because it's actually in a different parent. If any plugin does that, it will print an error. Although you can just do `queue_free()`, so probably not a problem.

So after more changes there is yet another compatibility breakage, and this time a rather major one. Since the main screen docks are no longer associated with a specific plugin, changing main screen tab no longer calls `make_visible()` and `selected_notify()`. I can add some super very hacky code to handle it for legacy plugins, but I'm not sure if it's worth it. It would be very ugly.

I think all main screen docks should be able to dock anywhere. The above image is a bundle of screenshots of UI setups I thought looked good after quickly modifying the source code. As you can see, it would allow to see both the 2D and 3D editors at once, which is currently only useful if a scene has both 2D and 3D nodes that aren't within Viewports (might be a bug), but still very promising for the future. It would also allow for viewing and editing script at the same time as viewing a scene, which is a feature that has been asked for a lot.

This is also good for users with only 1 monitor, as with this PR, main screen docks can only be made floating and they would therefore only benefit a little from this.

On a side note I think the Shader Editor should also benefit from Main Screen and Side docks but maybe that one could be in a follow-up PR, as it seems a bit out of scope.

> I think all main screen docks should be able to dock anywhere.

That's out of scope. This PR only adds the new dock slot, converts existing main screens and enables layouts that make sense right now. No main screen editor is really suited to be docked somewhere else right now. 2D and 3D editors are too wide to be used in side docks. They _might_ work at the bottom though, but if they require any changes for other layouts, it should be done in follow-ups.

> That's out of scope.

Agreed, I'll try to make a follow-up PR when I can then.

As for how they work currently, they work fine in the bottom docks, where they only suffer from low minimum height which can easily be fixed. The side docks suffer from the main screen docks' minimum width, which makes them way too wide for use with other docks in the same tab.

Now that main screen editors no longer need to be at main screen, I think they need some rework. For starters, I'd deprecated `_has_main_screen()` and instead introduce `_is_main_editor()` (or similar), which _effectively_ would work the same, but had different purpose.
Right now returning `true` in `_has_main_screen()` only makes sense if the plugin actually edits some objects. There is still a distinction between sub editors and main editors. And object can be edited only by single sub editor and single main editor. E.g. when you click a TileMapLayer node, it should be edited by TileMap (sub) editor, and 2D (main) editor, because it's also a CanvasItem. `_has_main_screen()` no longer means "placed at main screen", but differentiates main and sub editors.
I will do a follow-up once this PR is merged.

> It makes more sense because the engine wouldn't have those scenarios where a scene is selected but another script for a different scene is in the script view, which is very confusing:

I also think placing scene names at the top feels out of place, particularly when working in non-scene-related tabs like the Script tab or other `EditorPlugin` main screens.

This is part of why I've questioned the current design, where "SceneTabs" are essentially open-file tabs that span the entire editor regardless of context. An alternative worth considering: each `EditorPlugin` main screen manages its own set of open tabs, and the tab bar updates to reflect whichever main screen is currently active.

Under this model, switching to the Script tab would show no scene tabs at all. To view or switch between open scenes, you'd either navigate to the 2D/3D main screen and select a scene tab there, or use a kebab menu on the Scene Tree dock to switch between all currently open scenes without leaving your current context.

A slight alternative to the kebab on the dock is make it as a right click option on the main screen dock button that shows a popup of all open things of that editor type.

But that's just my $0.02.

These all have various platform and accessability concerns that would need evaluation.

One thing at the time, y'all. This is a pretty fundamental editor change by itself.

> The old main screen plugin workflow is deprecated. It's still supported, but compatibility might be broken in some edge cases

EditorInterface.get_editor_main_screen() no longer provides the main screen. That's not deprecated or backwards compatible. That's a hard API change.

How do we get the main editor screen now? This has broken our viewport live info panel for Terrain3D. Is there an alternate method for placing an info panel like GPU/frame info? Or a way to determine if the editor is in 1, 2, or 4 viewport mode? Or a way to directly get the Node3DEditorViewportContainer?
You can get the 3D editor directly with `EditorInterface.get_dock_by_name("3D")`. Accessing it via main screen is no longer valid, because it can be moved elsewhere.

Why does EditorInterface.get_editor_main_screen() still exist? It just fails silently, while providing a valid dummy node. It should either print a warning/error that it does nothing or be removed so the end user recognizes the API has changed.

> Why does EditorInterface.get_editor_main_screen() still exist? It's needed to make sure that the old main screen plugins still work the same as before. The deprecated note clarifies it. When a plugin implementing `_has_main_screen()` adds a node to the legacy "main screen", the editor automatically creates a dock for it.
